```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE)

# Load libraries
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(kableExtra)
library(janitor) # tabyl
library(ggplot2)

# wd
setwd("~/Desktop/ColumbiaPhD/research_projects/Lauren_menstrualmodelingmethods/menst_mod")  

# data

# self-reported irregularity
# BCFR irregularity data (Clue) -- has "ever irregular" variable : IRREGULAR_MENSES
bcfr_irr = read.csv("./data/yws_clue/ywsclue_repro.csv") 
# recode
bcfr_irrdata = bcfr_irr |>
  mutate(
    irr_ever = case_when(
      IRREGULAR_MENSES == 2 ~ 0, # NO: regular
      IRREGULAR_MENSES == 1 ~ 1, # YES: irregular (Eva said 1 is irregular)
      IRREGULAR_MENSES == 3 ~ NA # 3 = "don't know".(29)
    ), 
    irr_12mo = case_when(
      MENSES_STARS_AS_EXPECTED == 2 ~ 1, # 2: NO, period did not start on time, i.e. IRregular
      MENSES_STARS_AS_EXPECTED == 1 ~ 0, # 1: YES, period started on time/as expected i.e. REGULAR (coding is FLIPPED!!!! for these two vars... !)
      MENSES_STARS_AS_EXPECTED == 3 ~ NA # 3 = "don't know".
    )
  )

# skipTrack fits & generated stats
bcfryws_irr_nospot = read.csv("./skiptrack/data_clean/datasets_tosend/bcfryws_irr_nospot.csv")
bcfryws_irr_nospot_s = read.csv( "./skiptrack/data_clean/datasets_tosend/bcfryws_irr_nospot_s.csv")


# FIX CODING OF 12month irregularity::

bcfryws_irr_nospot = bcfryws_irr_nospot |>
  mutate(
    irr_12mo = case_when(
      irr_12mo == 0 ~ 0, # 2: NO, period did not start on time, i.e. IRregular
      irr_12mo == 1 ~ 1, # 1: YES, period started on time/as expected i.e. REGULAR (coding is FLIPPED!!!! for these two vars... !)
      irr_12mo == NA ~ NA # 3 = "don't know".
    )
  )
bcfryws_irr_nospot_s = bcfryws_irr_nospot_s |>
  mutate(
    irr_12mo = case_when(
      irr_12mo == 0 ~ 1, # 2: NO, period did not start on time, i.e. IRregular
      irr_12mo == 1 ~ 0, # 1: YES, period started on time/as expected i.e. REGULAR (coding is FLIPPED!!!! for these two vars... !)
      irr_12mo == NA ~ NA # 3 = "don't know".
    )
  )
```

## 1. Self-Reported Irregularity Measures
### Ever vs. 12-month irregularity

Full BCFR/YWS dataset: `n = (`r length(unique(bcfr_irr$PersonID))`)`

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# bcfr_irr data

# 2x2 table

bcfr_irrdata1 = bcfr_irrdata |>
  mutate(
    irr_everL = case_when(
      irr_ever == 0 ~ "reg",
      irr_ever == 1 ~ "irr_ever"
    ), 
    irr_12moL = case_when(
      irr_12mo == 0 ~ "reg", # regular
      irr_12mo == 1 ~ "irr_12mo"
    )
  )

bcfr_irrdata2 = table(bcfr_irrdata1 |> select(irr_everL, irr_12moL), useNA = c("ifany"))
bcfr_irrdata2 = addmargins(bcfr_irrdata2)

bcfr_irrdata2 |> 
  kbl(caption = "Counts") |> 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F, position = "center") |> 
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)

# now proportions, without NA

bcfr_irrdata3 = table(bcfr_irrdata1 |> select(irr_everL, irr_12moL))
bcfr_irrdata3 = prop.table(bcfr_irrdata3) * 100

bcfr_irrdata3 = addmargins(bcfr_irrdata3)

bcfr_irrdata3 |> 
  kbl(caption = "Percentages") |> 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F, position = "center") |> 
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(bcfr_irrdata1 |> filter(!is.na(irr_12mo), !is.na(irr_ever)), mapping = aes(irr_ever, irr_12mo)) + 
  geom_point() +   
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # Adds the linear regression line (loess, not linear, but you get the idea...)
```

## 2. Self-Reported Irregularity Measures vs. Variance of Cycle Lengths in Clue Data

Clue dataset: `n = (`r length(unique(bcfryws_irr_nospot$PersonID))`)`

```{r}
# Clue df with 1 obs per person
clue_1obs = bcfryws_irr_nospot_s |> group_by(PersonID) |> summarise(irr_ever = mean(irr_ever),
                                                                    irr_12mo = mean(irr_12mo),
                                                                    cycle_var = mean(cycle_var),
                                                                    mean_tau = mean(mean_tau))
# to calculate means across INDIVIDUALS, not weighted by # cycle lengths observed i.e. j!!
```

### Ever Irregularity vs. `var(cycle_len)`

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(clue_1obs |> filter(!is.na(irr_ever)), mapping = aes(irr_ever, cycle_var)) + 
  geom_point() +   
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # Adds the linear regression line ( linear not loess, but you get the idea...)
```

Mean cycle variance by ever-irregular status:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
var_ever = clue_1obs |> group_by(irr_ever) |> summarize(mean_var = mean(cycle_var))

var_ever |> 
  kbl(caption = "Mean cycle variance by ever-irr status") |> 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F, position = "center") |> 
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

### 12-month Irregularity vs. `var(cycle_len)`


```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(clue_1obs |> filter(!is.na(irr_12mo)), mapping = aes(irr_12mo, cycle_var)) + 
  geom_point() +   
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # Adds the linear regression line (loess, not linear, but you get the idea...)
```

Mean cycle variance by ever-irregular status:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
var_12mo = clue_1obs |> group_by(irr_12mo) |> summarize(mean_var = mean(cycle_var))

var_12mo |> 
  kbl(caption = "Mean cycle variance by 12mo-irr status") |> 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F, position = "center") |> 
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

## 3.Variance vs. $\tau_i$ (SkipTrack)

Clue dataset: `n = (`r length(unique(bcfryws_irr_nospot$PersonID))`)`

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(clue_1obs, mapping = aes(cycle_var, mean_tau)) + 
  geom_point() +   
  geom_smooth(method = "loess") + # loess -- expect this to be non-linear!!
  ggtitle("var(cycle length) in raw data vs. tau_i (precision) estimated for logNormal underlying dist")

# you know what... it DOES kind of look like an upside down logNormal!...but it looks odd for sure LOL -- maybe the lognormal is BECAUSE there are so many ppl crunched over there i.e. skewed dist!! : 0 : D

ggplot(clue_1obs |> filter(cycle_var<500), mapping = aes(cycle_var, mean_tau)) + 
  geom_point() +   
  geom_smooth(method = "loess") # loess -- expect this to be non-linear!!
```

If we reverse-transform tau_i values to "variance" as we would expect in the data, if a) all c_ijs = 1 & b) all individuals were identical i.e. no hierarchical/Bayesian pooling:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# re = reverse engineer
tau_var = bcfryws_irr_nospot_s |> group_by(PersonID) |> 
  mutate(var_tau_re = (exp(1/mean(mean_tau)) - 1) * exp(2 * log(mean(cycle_len)) + 1/mean(mean_tau))) # equation to recapture var from tau_i (precision) in lognormal underlying dist; note that mean cycle length has to be on the log scale, from the lognormal dist 

# *** [technically, would need the true underlying mu_i to capture this (not the mean(cycle_len) in the data!) -- that is why this is just a HEURISTIC check ***]

# Clue df with 1 obs per person
tau_1obs = tau_var |> group_by(PersonID) |> summarise(cycle_var = mean(cycle_var),
                                                      var_tau_re = mean(var_tau_re))
# to calculate means across INDIVIDUALS, not weighted by # cycle lengths observed i.e. j!!

ggplot(tau_1obs, mapping = aes(cycle_var, var_tau_re)) + 
  geom_point() +   
  geom_smooth(method = "loess")  + 
  geom_smooth (method = "lm", color = "red")+
  ggtitle("Variance of raw cycle lengths in data vs. 'reverse-engineered' variance from tau_i") +
  labs(caption = "We would expect these to align IF a) skipTrack estimated the \n mean cycle length in the data to be the true underlying cycle length for each individual, \n i.e. it found no evidence of skipped cycles! & b) the true cycle lengths *were* logNormally \n distributed [& a host of other modeling/functional form & measurement assumptions, ofc]. \n Therefore, the deviations from y = x are interesting & expected.")

# this makes sense!! i.e. these are roughlyyyyy aligned, but there are some cases when the model REALLY thinks that there are reporting malfunctions, and those data points are where tau_i super does not align with cycle variance in the raw data!

ggplot(tau_1obs |> filter(cycle_var<500), mapping = aes(cycle_var, var_tau_re)) + 
  geom_point() +   
  geom_smooth(method = "loess")  + 
  geom_smooth (method = "lm", color = "red")+
  ggtitle("Variance of raw cycle lengths in data vs. 'reverse-engineered' variance from tau_i") +
  labs(caption = "Here, where the variance in cycle lengths is much less extreme (i.e. less likely to have skipped cycles under skipTrack assumptions), tau_i and cycle_var approach y~x")
```

## 5. $\tau_i$ vs. $mean(c_{ij})$ (SkipTrack) in Clue Data

*Not necessary or as relevant to the project, but useful for understanding when/how/why $\tau_i$ deviates from `var(cycle_len)`, i.e. what skipTrack is telling us*

Clue dataset: `n = (`r length(unique(bcfryws_irr_nospot$PersonID))`)`

```{r, echo=FALSE}
mean_cij = bcfryws_irr_nospot_s |> group_by(PersonID) |> mutate(mean_cij_i = mean(cij_mean)) # mean cij per individual i, whereas cij_mean is the mean of the cij posterior for each ij observation

mean_cij = mean_cij |> group_by(PersonID) |> summarise(mean_cij_i = mean(mean_cij_i), # should condense to a single value, since they all have the same value for each personID -- applies for all 3 vars
                                                      PersonID = mean(PersonID),
                                                      mean_tau = mean(mean_tau))

ggplot(mean_cij, mapping = aes(mean_cij_i, mean_tau)) + 
  geom_point() +   
  geom_smooth(method = "loess") + # loess -- expect this to be non-linear!!
  ggtitle("mean_cij vs. tau_i (precision) estimated for logNormal underlying dist")

# huh -- no super obvious tradeoff, to my eyes, except that this does look vaguely lognormal except for the outliers? probably a good sign for the model, but again -- frankly hard to tell without a validation dataset
```
